question: The H.C.F. and the L.C.M. of two numbers are 11 and 495, respectively. If one of the numbers is 55, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that the product of two numbers is equal to the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M.

⇒ First Number × Second Number = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

⇒ 55 × Second Number = 11 × 495

⇒ Second Number = (11 × 495) ÷ 55

⇒ Second Number = 495 ÷ 5 = 99

**∴ The correct answer is 99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

H.C.F. of two numbers = 11

L.C.M. of two numbers = 495

One of the numbers = 55

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = Product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M.

**Calculation:**

Let the second number be x.

⇒ 55 × x = 11 × 495

⇒ x = (11 × 495) ÷ 55

⇒ x = 495 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 99

**∴ The correct answer is 99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

H.C.F. and L.C.M. of Fractions

H.C.F. = (H.C.F. of Numerators) ÷ (L.C.M. of Denominators)
L.C.M. = (L.C.M. of Numerators) ÷ (H.C.F. of Denominators)

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their H.C.F. is exactly 1. The L.C.M. of co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Divisibility Property

The H.C.F. of any given set of numbers is always a direct factor of their L.C.M.
